### Tree select
Choose one or more leaves from a tree using the keyboard or pointer.

Component ID: `tree-select`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/tree-select.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/tree-select.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.20.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.20.0

Contract SHA-256: `991ed04b88340765f86b7e3424e3cc3cc80c0125d51b7c8501c031ce22a32884`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Public JavaScript exports: `TreeSelect`. See the [API index](../references/api-index.md).

Example: A destination field with continents, countries and cities takes a data-tree select whose cities are the leaves; a field of five countries stays a select.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Support: A native select[data-tree] whose flat options name their parent's value in data-parent; a role="tree" popup with the ARIA tree keyboard contract over visible, enabled rows, mirrored under RTL; single or native multiple independent leaf choices, with branches normalized out of multiple selection; branch options disabled while it runs; optional single/multiple leaf search retaining ancestor paths and restoring pre-query expansion; refresh() preserving the query, expansion baseline and focus.

Web adaptation: TreeSelect extends FormSelect, so the native select keeps the form value, reset, validity and disabled state. The popup is a ul role="tree" inside the Menu surface, one list below the rows Menu styles, named as the field is. Search reuses the labelled dialog/search/status controls around that tree without a listbox wrapper.

Known boundary: No choosable branch; the field shows leaf text, not ancestor paths.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#tree-select).

#### Contract

Choose leaves from options nested as a tree, expanded with the keyboard or pointer.

A native `<select data-tree>` holds flat `<option>`s. A child names its parent option's value in `data-parent`; an option without one is a root, and an option another option names is a branch. `AutoInit()` starts every `select[data-tree]` as `TreeSelect`, a FormSelect subclass, so the field, labels, validation messages and reset work as in a select. The native select still owns the form value, reset, validity and the disabled state. HTML cannot nest `<optgroup>`s, so nesting comes only from `data-parent`.

The popup is a `<ul role="tree">` inside the Menu surface, named as the field is: its `aria-labelledby`, then its `aria-label`, then its labels. Branch rows have `aria-expanded` and hold their children in a `ul[role="group"]`; leaf rows have `aria-selected`. Branches start collapsed. In default mode, opening reveals and focuses the first chosen enabled leaf, or the first enabled row; search mode focuses its separate search field.

#### Syntax

```html
<div class="field">
  <select id="place" name="place" data-tree>
    <option value="" disabled selected>Choose a place</option>
    <option value="europe" disabled>Europe</option>
    <option value="france" data-parent="europe" disabled>France</option>
    <option value="paris" data-parent="france">Paris</option>
    <option value="lyon" data-parent="france">Lyon</option>
    <option value="spain" data-parent="europe">Spain</option>
    <option value="asia" disabled>Asia</option>
    <option value="tokyo" data-parent="asia">Tokyo</option>
  </select>
  <label for="place">Place</label>
</div>
```

#### Methods

- `.refresh()`: Rebuilds the tree from the native options after a page adds, removes or changes them. Without search, branches whose value is still there stay open. An active query is reapplied without overwriting its saved expansion baseline. While open, focus stays on a surviving enabled visible row, moves to an enabled visible row, or returns to search when none remains.
- `.getSelectedValues()`: The selected native option values in option order, as in FormSelect.
- `.destroy()`: Removes the tree and its listeners, restores the branch options' `disabled` attributes and the native select.

#### Also documented

The Tree select section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Multiple leaves, Tree search, Properties.

#### Rules

- `tree-select-needs-native-options`: Put data-tree on a native <select>, optionally with multiple. Nest flat options only through data-parent naming the parent option value. An <optgroup> cannot nest, and data-parent needs a select with data-tree.
- `option-has-selected-state`: role=option promises a selection state. Without aria-selected the listbox never says which entry is chosen.
